ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a voltage source labeled 20 V, with the upper end positive; the upper end of the voltage source is connected through a 10 Ω series resistor to the left port of the two-port network. The middle of the two-port is labeled [Z]. The left-port current I1 arrow points into the interior of the two-port, and the port voltage V1 is positive at the top and negative at the bottom. The right port is connected to a load RL, the arrow of the port current I2 also points into the interior of the two-port, and the port voltage V2 is positive at the top and negative at the bottom. Reasoning: It is known that the z parameters are z11=40 Ω, z12=60 Ω, z21=80 Ω, z22=100 Ω, so the two-port equations are V1=40I1+60I2, V2=80I1+100I2. From the external circuit on the left side, the port voltage V1 equals the source voltage minus the voltage drop across the 10 Ω resistor: V1=20-10I1. The right-side load RL=20 Ω is connected to port 2, and I2 is defined as flowing into the two-port, so the load current direction is opposite to I2; therefore V2=-20I2. Simultaneous equations: 40I1+60I2=20-10I1, giving 50I1+60I2=20. Also 80I1+100I2=-20I2, giving 80I1+120I2=0. Simplified as 5I1+6I2=2, and 2I1+3I2=0. From the second equation I1=-1.5I2; substituting into the first equation gives -7.5I2+6I2=2, that is, I2=-4/3 A, therefore I1=2 A. The load voltage V2=-20I2=26.6667 V. The average power P=V2^2/RL=(26.6667)^2/20=35.5556 W, approximately 35.55 W.
